extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent applicants/agents (PCT practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining and documenting unity of invention in PCT international applications, including Markush groups, intermediate/final products, invitations to pay additional search fees, telephonic practice, protests, and related search-reporting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept. The requirement is fulfilled only when there is a technical relationship among those inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. The determination shall be made without regard to whether the inventions are claimed in separate claims or as alternatives within a single claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression 'special technical features' means those technical features that define a contribution which each of the claimed inventions, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art. When claims are directed to multiple categories (product, process, apparatus, use), the first invention of the category first mentioned and the first recited invention of each other category related thereto will be considered the 'main invention'. If no additional fees are paid timely, the international search/examination will be based on the main invention (PCT Article 17(3)(a), 37 CFR 1.475(d)). Follow form paragraphs (e.g., 18.05-18.07) when making lack-of-unity actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group alternatives — similar nature criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: When a single claim defines alternatives of a Markush group, the requirement of technical interrelationship and same or corresponding special technical features is considered met when the alternatives are of a similar nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For chemical-compound Markush groupings, alternatives are regarded as of similar nature where (A) all alternatives have a common property or activity; and (B) either (1) a common structure is present (a significant structural element is shared by all alternatives) OR (2) all alternatives belong to a recognized class of chemical compounds in the art. 'Significant structural element' may occupy a large portion of structures or be a structurally distinctive portion in view of prior art and be essential to the common property/activity. 'Recognized class' means expectation from knowledge in the art that members will behave similarly (interchangeable for intended result). The fact alternatives are differently classified should not alone justify lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group alternatives — when lack of unity found
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and form-paragraph headings for finding that chemical alternatives of a Markush group are not of a similar nature and therefore lack unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific form paragraphs (18.07.03, 18.07.03a-c) to state why alternatives lack a common property/activity, lack a common structure, or do not belong to a recognized class. When an alternative of a Markush group is shown to be not novel over prior art, the unity question should be reconsidered by the examiner. Provide reasoning and cite prior art when asserting that a shared technical feature does not make a contribution over the prior art (18.07.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity between intermediate and final products
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is present between intermediate and final products when two conditions are fulfilled: (A) the intermediate and final products have the same essential structural element (basic chemical structures are the same OR chemically closely interrelated with the intermediate incorporating an essential structural element into the final product); and (B) the intermediate and final products are technically interrelated (final product is manufactured directly from the intermediate or separated by a small number of intermediates all containing the same essential structural element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity may be accepted even when structures are unknown (e.g., one known intermediate and a final product of unknown structure) if there is sufficient evidence that they are technically closely interrelated (e.g., intermediate contains same essential element). Different intermediate products used in different processes for the same final product may be accepted if they share the same essential structural element. Intermediates and final products shall not be separated by an intermediate which is not new. If the same application claims different intermediates for different structural parts of the final product, unity is not present. When families of compounds are claimed, each intermediate should correspond to a compound claimed in the final family, but families need not be absolutely congruent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of additional inventions when no additional fees paid
rubrics_metrics.description: If little or no additional search effort is required, the examiner may, for reasons of economy, search one or more additional inventions without payment of additional fees while making the search for the main invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international search for such additional inventions must be completed in any further classification units relevant when additional fees are paid. Examiner should consider the time needed to create the written opinion as well as perform the search when deciding whether to request additional fees. If total additional work does not justify requesting additional fees, all results may be included in the international search report and written opinion while still stating the finding of lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to pay additional fees (Form PCT/ISA/206) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA finds lack of unity, the applicant is informed by communication preceding issuance of the international search report and written opinion that contains an invitation to pay additional search fees, specifying reasons, identifying separate inventions, and indicating the number and amount of fees (PCT Rules 40.1, 40.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA should set out a logically presented, technical reasoning containing the basic considerations behind the finding of lack of unity (PCT Rule 40.1). The invitation sets a one-month time limit for response; extensions are not permitted. The ISA cannot consider the application withdrawn for lack of unity nor invite amendments in this communication. Additional fees are payable directly to the ISA conducting the search. Nonpayment results in portions remaining unsearched (which may be considered by national examiners later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation content for invitation to pay additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: On Form PCT/ISA/206 the examiner should indicate number of inventions claimed, which particular claims cover each invention, explain why the application lacks unity, and state total amount of additional fees required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims found to be unsearchable under PCT Article 17(2)(b) are excluded; unsearchable claims include: (A) subject matter not required to be searched by ISA (see MPEP §1843.02); (B) claims for which a meaningful search cannot be carried out (MPEP §1843.03); (C) multiple dependent claims not complying with PCT Rule 6.4(a) (MPEP §1843.03). Use appropriate form-paragraphs and provide clear identification of groups/claims using Roman numerals or species identifiers as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephonic unity practice (telephone payment of additional fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone practice may be used to allow applicants to pay additional fees if: (A) applicant or legal representative has a USPTO deposit account; (B) applicant or representative orally agrees to charge the additional fees to the account; and (C) a complete record of the telephone conversation is included with the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone record must include examiner's name, authorizing attorney's name, date, inventions for which additional fees paid, and deposit account number and amount. Examiner must orally inform applicant there is no right to protest lack of unity for inventions for which no additional fee has been paid and must advise that any protest to lack of unity or amount of fee must be filed in writing no later than one month from mailing date of international search report. If applicant refuses or lacks deposit account, send a written invitation using Form PCT/ISA/206. When telephonic practice used, document the holding of lack of unity using USPTO/299 telephone memorandum form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and headings for lack of unity actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized form paragraphs (e.g., 18.05–18.07.03c, 18.06, 18.06.01, 18.06.02) provide headings, group listings, and specified language for declaring lack of unity and identifying groups of claims (groups I, II, III etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin all lack-of-unity actions during the international phase with the required heading (¶18.05 / ¶18.07). Use form paragraphs to list groups of claims and categories (product/process/apparatus/use) and to explain why groups lack the same or corresponding technical feature. Use examiner notes in each form paragraph for insertion instructions and examples. For applications with claims to different categories, unity may still exist only for certain allowed category combinations (see 37 CFR 1.475(b) and enumerated combinations such as product + process specially adapted to manufacture it, product + use, process + apparatus, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure against payment of additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Administrative Instructions Section 502 and 37 CFR 1.477, an applicant who disagrees with a lack-of-unity holding may pay additional fees under protest, accompanied by request for refund and a reasoned statement explaining disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests are examined by the Director or designee; if found justified, additional fees or a portion are refunded. The protest must accompany payment of the additional search fees (no ISA/US protest fee required). Applicant may request that the protest and decision be transmitted with the international search report to designated Offices; notify ISA before issuance or otherwise notify International Bureau. Technology Center Director decides protests at USPTO; if protest unjustified, provide clear concise explanation (Form PCT/ISA/212).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decision on protest (Form PCT/ISA/212) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PCT/ISA/212 is used by the Technology Center to inform applicant of decision regarding a protest on payment of additional fees concerning unity of invention; Form must be signed by a TC Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If decision box indicating protest unjustified is checked, provide a clear and concise explanation as to why the protest was found unjustified; because space is limited, attach supplemental sheets when necessary. The form is signed by a TC Director (MPEP §1002.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity for nucleotide sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences encoding the same protein are considered to satisfy the unity of invention standard and will continue to be examined together under 37 CFR 1.475 and 1.499 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples concerning unity involving biotechnological inventions are in Chapter 10 of the International Search and Preliminary Examination Guidelines (available from WIPO). When claimed subject matter does not involve the same or corresponding special technical features, additional fees are required to maintain claims in the same application (37 CFR 1.476(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and citation of patent documents in search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must cite references in accordance with Administrative Instructions Sections 503 and 611 and WIPO Standard ST.14, including indication of two-letter country code and standard kind code (WIPO Standard ST.16) when preparing international search reports, written opinions, and international preliminary examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents/published patent applications list elements in order: (A) Office two-letter code (WIPO ST.3); (B) document number as given by Office; (C) kind of document (per ST.16); (D) name of patentee/applicant; (E) date of publication (or corrected-document issuance date, INID 48) and any supplementary correction code (INID 15); (F) where applicable, pages/columns/lines/paragraph numbers or figures. Nonpatent literature documents are Code N. Examples: JP 10-105775 A (NCR INTERNATIONAL INC.) 24 April 1998 paragraphs 26 to 30; US 5,635,683 A (MCDERMOTT, R. M. et al.) 03 June 1997, column 7, lines 21 to 40. Use WIPO Standard ST.16 for kind codes and ST.3 for country/entity codes; consult MPEP §901.04(a) for US-specific code guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard codes and country codes (WIPO ST.16 and ST.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO Standard ST.16 provides standard codes distinguishing kinds of patent documents; WIPO Standard ST.3 provides two-letter country/organization codes used when identifying patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ST.16 subdivides kinds into mutually exclusive groups (including code groups for previously/currently published kinds). Part 7.3 of ST.16 gives examples and samples. ST.3 lists two-letter codes for states/entities (Annex I) and historical/changed codes (Annex II). Use letter codes when numerical designations are not provided on documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking into account results of earlier search (PCT Rule 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant has requested the ISA to take into account results of an earlier search (Rule 4.12) and has complied with Rule 12bis.1: (i) if earlier search was by same ISA or same Office, the ISA shall, to the extent possible, take those results into account; (ii) if earlier search was by another ISA or Office, the ISA may take those results into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.104 and MPEP §1819 discuss international-type searches. An international-type search is made in all national applications filed on/after June 1, 1978; applicants may request an international-type search during national examination upon written request and payment of fee. When considering earlier results, the ISA should be guided by whether the earlier search was performed by the same authority and by Rule 12bis.1 compliance.
